summary: Verified Google OAuth 403 fix. Backend POST /api/auth/google returns 401 gracefully on invalid code. Callback shows helpful data-testid='google-callback-message' for access_denied (mentions 403 + publish/test user) and generic 'Sign-in failed, redirecting…' for invalid code, then redirects to /login. Email OTP regression PASS. CRITICAL DISCOVERY: main agent's assumption that the 403 is a Google-side 'Testing mode' issue is likely WRONG — the running frontend was sending client_id=undefined because it had not been restarted after REACT_APP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID was set in frontend/.env. After I restarted the frontend, the Google URL now contains the real client_id. This is very likely the root cause of the user's 403.

integration_issues.issue: Frontend served client_id=undefined in the Google authorization URL (env var REACT_APP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID was in /app/frontend/.env but the running CRA process had been started before it was added / hadn't been reloaded). This causes Google to reject the request (invalid_request → often surfaced as HTTP 400/403 in the browser) which perfectly matches the user's 'Error 403' report. Restarting the frontend fixed the URL to include the real client_id. This is the most probable ACTUAL root cause of the user report — not the 'OAuth consent screen Testing mode' theory.

action_items: IMPORTANT: The 'Error 403' the user reported is very likely NOT the Google Cloud Console 'Testing mode' issue as previously diagnosed. It was almost certainly caused by REACT_APP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID not being loaded by the running frontend process (client_id=undefined in the outgoing Google URL). I restarted the frontend and the URL is now correct. Please confirm with the user whether the 403 is gone after this restart.
Consider adding a guard in Login.jsx: if !clientId, show an actionable error toast ('OAuth client not configured') instead of navigating to Google with client_id=undefined.
OPTIONAL: The graceful access_denied message is currently English only; consider localising it via getT(lang) like the rest of the page.
critical_code_review_comments: Login.jsx googleLogin() has no fallback/guard when REACT_APP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID is undefined — silently sends 'undefined' as client_id. Add: if (!clientId) { toast.error('Google login not configured'); return; }
GoogleCallback.jsx: fixed message text is English; app is Italian-first. Consider using getT(lang).
Backend /api/auth/google correctly returns 401 with generic detail — good, no 500 leaks; error is logged server-side.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 4 UI scenarios pass after frontend restart)

test_credentials: Not needed — Google auth tests do not require a real login. QA session (test_session_qa_01) not used.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 5 requested checks pass: (1) Google URL built correctly with client_id, redirect_uri=/auth/google, response_type=code, scope=openid email profile; (2) /auth/google?error=access_denied shows the 403/publish/test-user message via data-testid=google-callback-message and redirects to /login in ~2.6s; (3) /auth/google?code=fakecode123 shows 'Sign-in failed, redirecting…' and redirects to /login (~2s); (4) POST /api/auth/google with fake code returns HTTP 401 detail='Google authentication failed'; (5) Email OTP flow still works — email button reveals data-testid=login-email-input. IMPORTANT gotcha for next agent: frontend must be restarted after any change to /app/frontend/.env (REACT_APP_*), otherwise CRA serves stale env values.
rca of the issue: RCA of the reported 403: The frontend process was serving a JS bundle where process.env.REACT_APP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID resolved to undefined, so window.location.href became https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?client_id=undefined&... — Google's OAuth endpoint rejects such requests and the browser/user sees an error (commonly '403 access blocked' / 'Error 400: invalid_request'). Reproduction (pre-fix): opened /login in Chromium with route interception, clicked data-testid='login-google-button', captured navigation URL → literally 'client_id=undefined'. Mitigation applied: sudo supervisorctl restart frontend → CRA re-read /app/frontend/.env → URL now contains the real client_id (411367328532-e5bfa20v...apps.googleusercontent.com). Recommended permanent fix: add a client-side guard in Login.jsx googleLogin() so a missing client_id fails loudly instead of silently forwarding 'undefined' to Google.
